title: Cargo Floor Panel and Intercostal — Puncture Repair with a Bonded Insert

issue.reason: Issue B. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: Repair of a puncture or crushed core in a cargo floor panel using a bonded insert, with the intercostal check that decides whether the underlying structure has also been loaded.

sections.purpose: This repair restores the load-carrying capability and the sealing of a cargo floor panel that has been punctured or whose core has been crushed by a dropped load, and defines the check of the underlying intercostal.
sections.damage_assessment: Sound the panel around the visible damage with a tap hammer and mark the boundary of the crushed core, which is normally larger than the visible puncture. Measure the damage across two axes and record its position relative to the nearest seat track and floor beam. Damage up to 150 millimetres across may be repaired by this scheme. Damage larger than that, damage over a floor beam, or damage where the panel has been pushed down onto the intercostal below, requires an engineering assessment. Always lift the adjacent panel and inspect the intercostal underneath, because a dropped load heavy enough to punch the panel will usually have deformed it as well.
sections.repair_procedure: Remove the damaged panel from the compartment. Cut out the crushed core to a circular boundary at least 25 millimetres beyond the sounded limit, keeping the lower skin intact. Remove the core debris and clean the cavity with the approved solvent. Do a tap test of the cut boundary and confirm that the remaining core is sound. Fit the potting compound and let it cure. Machine the recess to accept the insert and check the depth at four points. Bond the insert using the film given on repair drawing RD-53-50-13-908 and cure it under pressure with the heater blanket. After cure, restore the upper skin with the doubler shown on sheet 2, fastened with the anchor nuts AGS661650K8 and the tension head bolts EN330176-8B into the cleat D5350130671217. Where the intercostal below has deformed, renew the splice plate ES657922-93 before the panel is refitted. Refit the panel, torque the seat track fasteners and check the floor level with the straight edge.
sections.inspection_requirements: The repair is life limited to 25000 flight cycles from the date of embodiment. Do a tap test of the insert boundary at every C check and a detailed visual inspection of the underlying intercostal every 10000 flight cycles. Any disbond at the insert boundary, or any evidence that the panel is moving relative to the intercostal, invalidates the repair. Report the repair so that it is recorded against the aircraft and reflected in the cargo compartment load limits if more than three repairs are present in one compartment.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: Puncture or crushed core up to 150 millimetres across, not over a floor beam, with the lower skin intact and no deformation of the intercostal below.
